headline: Colibrì runs 1.5-TB AI model on 25GB RAM, shows promise for local AI
summary: A novel proof-of-concept, Colibrì, enables a frontier-level 1.5-TB AI model to run on just 25GB of RAM, using a modest CPU and virtual NVMe drive. This approach shows significant promise for local AI setups, despite current performance limitations.
details: Italian engineer Vincenzo (JustVugg) created Colibrì to run the 744-billion-parameter 1.5-TB GLM-5.2 model. It operates on a modest CPU, 25 GB of RAM, and a 1 GB/s virtual NVMe drive, making frontier-level AI accessible on limited hardware.

Currently, Colibrì's speed is 0.05 to 0.1 tokens per second, too slow for practical real-time conversation. While higher-end setups improve figures, they still fall short of the 20-30 tokens per second needed for fluid interaction.

GLM-5.2 is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model, known for its frontier-level capabilities and excellent answer quality. Colibrì achieves its low memory footprint by loading the model in slices to RAM, a complex but effective method.

MoE models activate specific 'expert' sub-models per token, not per entire query. Colibrì exploits this architecture by repeatedly loading and unloading only the necessary experts. This allows large models to run on less powerful machines, albeit with a significant performance penalty.

Colibrì's expert-selection code is a simple C file, and the GLM-5.2 model is quantized to reduce its initial size. The main bottlenecks are NVMe storage speed and memory bandwidth, followed by CPU core limitations.

As a proof-of-concept, Colibrì does not yet run on GPUs, though data shuffling would still be a major constraint. The project is new but gaining popularity, with Vincenzo actively collecting benchmark data and implementing fixes.
